tldr: None of the direct Canadian competitors (CIBC, RBC, TD, Scotiabank, BMO, Wealthsimple, EQ Bank, Tangerine) made a tracked move today. The news was dominated by Brazil's B3 pushing low-cost access to the Anthropic IPO, Latin American fintechs pushing into investing and banking licences, and a run of outages and security incidents at large banks and exchanges.
themes: Fractional, low-minimum access to hot IPOs and assets

highlights.headline: B3 listed an Anthropic BDR (ANTH34) for under R$100, trading at the same time as the Nasdaq IPO.
highlights.why: Brazilian retail investors get same-day, small-ticket access to a marquee US IPO. Canadian self-directed customers may come to expect the same, so the team should check how Simplii handles IPO access and fractional or CDR-style products.

highlights.headline: Mercado Pago launched CEDEAR investing, letting users buy US stocks in pesos from inside its app, and is taking on Cocos.
highlights.why: A payments and wallet app is turning into a full retail broker. This is the same convergence that Wealthsimple and Kalshi represent, and it raises the bar for in-app investing from a bank account.

highlights.headline: Kalshi is buying broker FB Securities to launch stock and ETF trading, and Dave has applied for a US national bank charter. Nubank also gained a Brazilian banking licence.
highlights.why: Prediction markets, neobanks and fintechs are all moving to own the regulated stack and offer broader product sets. Competition for primary-account and trading relationships will come from non-traditional players.

highlights.headline: Itaú had app, login and Pix failures, Wells Fargo and Chase had outages, Banco do Brasil confirmed a customer data leak, and Mercado Bitcoin resumed trading after a US$49M hack.
highlights.why: Reliability and security remain key reasons customers distrust or leave a bank. Simplii should check its own incident communication, status transparency and scam-warning playbooks.
